goal: Stops the wallet from producing SIGHASH_SINGLE signatures when there is no output at the input's index.
Closes a footgun where such signatures stay valid even if outputs are later reordered or swapped, letting funds be redirected without the signer's consent.
Applies the fix to walletprocesspsbt, which previously lacked the guard that legacy signing already had.

agreement: Concept ACK and full ACK, both without objection (l0rinc, achow101).
No standing criticism or disagreement found in the discussion.

categories.name: wallet
why: P1 because an unpatched signer can produce a SIGHASH_SINGLE signature that stays valid after outputs are swapped, letting funds be redirected without the owner's consent.
Fund safety is the top priority for this category and this closes a signature-malleability footgun that affects any PSBT signing flow, not just the fixed SignTransaction path.

result.summary: This PR moves the existing SIGHASH_SINGLE-with-missing-output guard into CreateSig itself, so both SignTransaction and SignPSBTInput (used by walletprocesspsbt) refuse to produce a detached signature when there is no output at the input's index. Previously only SignTransaction had this check; PSBT signing lacked it, letting walletprocesspsbt sign such inputs. A functional test covering legacy, bech32, and bech32m address types is added, plus two unrelated test-robustness tweaks (picking a specific coinbase UTXO instead of listunspent()[0]).
result.problem: SIGHASH_SINGLE with no corresponding output commits to nothing (fixed sighash 1 for legacy, zeroed hashOutputs for segwit v0), so the resulting signature stays valid even if the transaction's outputs are later reordered or swapped. This can let an attacker redirect funds without the wallet owner's consent, and the walletprocesspsbt RPC path did not guard against it even though raw signing already did.

result.card: This PR closes a fund-safety footgun: a SIGHASH_SINGLE signature for an input with no matching output commits to nothing, so it stays valid even after outputs are swapped, letting funds be redirected without the signer's consent (per the PR description and linked issue #35977). It moves the existing guard (already present in raw SignTransaction) into CreateSig so the PSBT signing path (walletprocesspsbt) is also protected, and adds a functional test across legacy, bech32, and bech32m address types. Review state is Ready; the only full ACK (achow101) predates a later force-push and should be re-confirmed, but no design questions are open. l0rinc gave Concept ACK and achow101 gave ACK, with no objections raised. No dependencies; it directly resolves open issue #35977.
